request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Completion was claimed without a relevant verification result.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Run the relevant checks, record their outcome, and report any unavailable check before making a success claim.",
    "description": "Use when reporting a completed code change or fix.",
    "name": "verify-before-claim"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "Verification needs a repeatable multi-step procedure, so a skill is justified."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":3,"justification":"It specifies concrete steps (run checks, record outcome, report unavailable checks before claiming success) but leaves 'relevant checks' undefined, so it doesn't pin down which commands or artifacts constitute proof."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":3,"justification":"The rule generalizes cleanly across any 'claim completion' scenario, but its phrasing ('run the relevant checks') is generic enough to risk becoming a platitude without an example of what counts as a check."},"trigger_quality":{"score":4,"justification":"'Use when reporting a completed code change or fix' is a real, situational trigger tied to a concrete moment (the completion report) rather than a vague always-on condition."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy body and description contain no project-, file-, or tool-specific nouns and would read the same in any codebase."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"This is a one-line standing behavioral rule ('verify before claiming success'), not a multi-step procedure with tools or branching logic, so a lighter-weight memory/rule entry would suffice more cheaply than packaging it as an invokable skill."}}

actionability.justification: It specifies concrete steps (run checks, record outcome, report unavailable checks before claiming success) but leaves 'relevant checks' undefined, so it doesn't pin down which commands or artifacts constitute proof.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The rule generalizes cleanly across any 'claim completion' scenario, but its phrasing ('run the relevant checks') is generic enough to risk becoming a platitude without an example of what counts as a check.

leakage.justification: The remedy body and description contain no project-, file-, or tool-specific nouns and would read the same in any codebase.

routing_fitness.justification: This is a one-line standing behavioral rule ('verify before claiming success'), not a multi-step procedure with tools or branching logic, so a lighter-weight memory/rule entry would suffice more cheaply than packaging it as an invokable skill.

trigger_quality.justification: 'Use when reporting a completed code change or fix' is a real, situational trigger tied to a concrete moment (the completion report) rather than a vague always-on condition.
